1. This repository contains no illegal content

The code, documentation, patches, and default prompts published by dsh-purge are not trojans, backdoors, unauthorized penetration tools, ransomware, or credential-stuffing scripts, nor are they attack payloads aimed at public networks or third-party systems. The project does not provide illegal content and does not instigate, organize, or assist in any illegal or criminal activity.

2. Local operations do not constitute external authorization

Applying patches, writing, rolling back, and uninstalling all take place within local files and local processes. These operations do not scan, probe, intrude into, or send attack traffic to any public host or unauthorized system, and this machine must not be used as a jump host.

If the plugin has update checks enabled, it may only access this plugin's own GitHub repository to verify the version. That access is unrelated to network attacks on third-party systems and must not be interpreted as authorization for external penetration testing.

3. Permitted scope of use

Use is permitted only in environments you can prove you are entitled to handle: the official Harness installed locally on a machine you administer; offline, local synthetic targets; cybersecurity exercise ranges for which the owner has issued lawful written authorization; and controlled environments in a compliant laboratory. Written authorization must correspond to specific targets, time, and scope. Entering only an organization name, or relying only on an oral statement, does not constitute authorization.

Targets without the owner's lawful written authorization, publicly reachable online systems, production services, and critical information infrastructure such as energy, transportation, water resources, finance, public services, and e-government systems must not be used as exercise targets.

4. Laws that must be complied with, by article and paragraph

Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 285(1): It is prohibited to violate state regulations and intrude into computer information systems in the fields of state affairs, national defense, and cutting-edge science and technology.

Article 285(2): It is prohibited to intrude into computer information systems other than those specified in the preceding paragraph, or to use other technical means to obtain data stored, processed, or transmitted in such systems, or to exercise illegal control over such systems.

Article 285(3): It is prohibited to provide programs or tools specially used for intruding into or illegally controlling computer information systems; providing programs or tools to others while knowing that they intend to intrude or illegally control is likewise prohibited.

Article 286(1): It is prohibited to delete, modify, add to, or interfere with the functions of a computer information system, causing the system to fail to operate normally.

Article 286(2): It is prohibited to delete, modify, or add to data and application programs stored, processed, or transmitted in a system.

Article 286(3): It is prohibited to intentionally create or spread destructive programs such as computer viruses that affect the normal operation of computer systems.

Article 287: It is prohibited to use computers to commit financial fraud, theft, embezzlement, misappropriation of public funds, theft of state secrets, or other crimes.

Article 287-1, paragraph 1, item (1): It is prohibited to establish websites or communication groups used for illegal or criminal activities such as fraud, teaching criminal methods, or producing or selling prohibited or controlled items.

Article 287-1, paragraph 1, item (2): It is prohibited to publish information about producing or selling drugs, firearms, obscene materials, or other prohibited or controlled items, or other illegal or criminal information.

Article 287-1, paragraph 1, item (3): It is prohibited to publish information for the purpose of committing fraud or other illegal or criminal activities.

Article 287-2: It is prohibited to knowingly provide technical support, advertising promotion, payment settlement, or other assistance to others who use information networks to commit crimes.

Article 253-1, paragraphs 1 and 3: It is prohibited to sell or provide citizens' personal information to others; it is prohibited to steal or otherwise unlawfully obtain citizens' personal information.

Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 13, paragraph 2: When using networks, one must not endanger cybersecurity, and must not use networks to engage in activities that endanger national security, honor, and interests; incite subversion of state power or overthrow of the socialist system; incite secession or undermine national unity; promote terrorism or extremism; promote ethnic hatred or ethnic discrimination; spread violence or obscene and pornographic information; fabricate or spread false information to disrupt economic and social order; or infringe on the reputation, privacy, intellectual property, or other lawful rights and interests of others.

Article 14: It is prohibited to use networks to engage in activities that endanger the physical and mental health of minors.

Article 29: It is prohibited to illegally intrude into others' networks, interfere with the normal functions of others' networks, or steal network data; it is prohibited to provide programs or tools specially used for intruding into networks, interfering with the normal functions of networks and protective measures, or stealing network data; when knowing that others are engaged in activities endangering cybersecurity, it is prohibited to provide them with technical support, advertising promotion, payment settlement, or other assistance.

Article 33: Critical information infrastructure in public communications and information services, energy, transportation, water resources, finance, public services, and e-government is subject to priority protection. Without lawful authorization, no one may intrude into, interfere with, or destroy it.

Article 46: It is prohibited to steal or otherwise unlawfully obtain personal information, and it is prohibited to unlawfully sell or unlawfully provide personal information to others.

Article 48: It is prohibited to establish websites or communication groups used for fraud, teaching criminal methods, producing or selling prohibited or controlled items, or other illegal or criminal activities; it is prohibited to use networks to publish information involving the above illegal or criminal activities.

Article 50: Electronic information sent and application software provided must not contain malicious programs, and must not contain information that laws or administrative regulations prohibit from being published or transmitted.

Data Security Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 8: Data processing activities must not endanger national security or the public interest, or harm the lawful rights and interests of individuals or organizations.

Article 32(1): Data must be collected by lawful and proper means; data must not be stolen or otherwise unlawfully obtained.

Article 32(2): Where laws or administrative regulations specify the purpose and scope of data collection and use, data may only be collected and used within that purpose and scope.

Article 51: Those who steal or otherwise unlawfully obtain data, or thereby harm the lawful rights and interests of individuals or organizations, shall be punished in accordance with relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 5: Personal information must be processed lawfully, properly, necessarily, honestly, and in good faith, and must not be processed by misleading, fraudulent, coercive, or other such means.

Article 6, paragraphs 1 and 2: Personal information must be processed for a clear and reasonable purpose and in a way directly related to that purpose, using methods that have the least impact on individual rights and interests; collection must be limited to the minimum scope necessary to achieve the processing purpose, and excessive collection is prohibited.

Article 10: It is prohibited to unlawfully collect, use, process, or transmit others' personal information, and to unlawfully buy, sell, provide, or disclose others' personal information; it is prohibited to engage in personal information processing activities that endanger national security or the public interest.

Article 13: Personal information must not be processed where none of the following applies: the individual's consent has been obtained; processing is necessary for concluding or performing a contract to which the individual is a party; processing is necessary for performing statutory duties or obligations; processing is necessary for responding to public health emergencies or protecting the life, health, and property of the individual in an emergency; processing is necessary for public-interest news reporting or public opinion supervision within a reasonable scope; the personal information has already been lawfully disclosed by the individual or otherwise lawfully disclosed; or other circumstances provided by laws or administrative regulations.

Articles 28 and 29: Biometrics, medical health, financial accounts, whereabouts and movement trajectories, and personal information of minors under the age of 14 are sensitive personal information. It must not be processed without a specific purpose, sufficient necessity, and strict protection measures, and without the individual's separate consent.

In addition, other currently effective laws, administrative regulations, and regulatory provisions, as well as the terms of service and abuse policies of the model used, must also be complied with.

5. Prohibited directions under this notice

Unauthorized access. It is prohibited to register as a target any organization, domain, address, public network system, production service, or critical information infrastructure for which there is no written authorization, and to scan, probe, intrude into, control, or send traffic to it. Corresponds to Criminal Law Article 285(1) and (2), and Cybersecurity Law Articles 29 and 33.

Damage and malicious programs. It is prohibited to delete, modify, add to, or interfere with others' system functions or the data and application programs therein; to create or spread viruses, ransomware, or other destructive programs; or to plant malicious programs in information or software. Corresponds to Criminal Law Article 286(1) to (3), and Cybersecurity Law Article 50.

Tools and assistance. It is prohibited to provide this project or this machine to others for intrusion, illegal control, or data theft; or, while knowing that the other party is committing a cybercrime, to still provide programs, tools, technical support, advertising promotion, or payment settlement. Corresponds to Criminal Law Article 285(3) and Article 287-2, and Cybersecurity Law Article 29.

Data. It is prohibited to steal, unlawfully collect, use beyond scope, disclose, sell, or provide to others business data, accounts, passwords, and other protected data. Corresponds to Data Security Law Articles 8, 32, and 51.

Personal information. It is prohibited to unlawfully collect, use, process, transmit, buy, sell, provide, or disclose others' personal information; to over-collect; to process by misleading, fraudulent, or coercive means; or to process biometric, medical health, financial account, whereabouts, and children's personal information without authorization. Corresponds to Criminal Law Article 253-1(1) and (3); Cybersecurity Law Article 46; Personal Information Protection Law Articles 5, 6, 10, 13, 28, and 29.

Fraud and illegal information. It is prohibited to establish or use websites or groups to commit fraud, teach criminal methods, or produce or sell prohibited or controlled items; to publish such information; or to use computers to commit fraud, theft, embezzlement, misappropriation of public funds, or theft of state secrets. Corresponds to Criminal Law Article 287, Article 287-1(1)(i) to (iii), and Cybersecurity Law Article 48.

Content. It is prohibited to generate or spread content that endangers national security, honor, and interests; to incite subversion or secession; to promote terrorism, extremism, or ethnic hatred; to spread violence, obscene or pornographic content, or gambling; to fabricate or spread false information that disrupts economic and social order; to infringe on reputation, privacy, or intellectual property; or to produce content that endangers the physical and mental health of minors. Corresponds to Cybersecurity Law Article 13, paragraph 2, and Article 14.

Spread of results. Records, asset information, and files created during exercises may remain only within the targets and time limits specified in the written authorization; they must not be handed to anyone not entitled to know them, and must not be repurposed beyond the authorization.
